title: General anesthetics block gap junctions, dissolving the higher-level Self

fields.label: Label
fields.value: General anesthetics block gap junctions, dissolving the higher-level Self

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: General anesthetics are gap-junction blockers, and on TAME's account shutting down electrical communication between cells makes the higher-level computational layer (the larger Self) disappear while the cells remain healthy; gap-junction blockers anesthetize organisms ranging from plants and Hydra to humans.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Consciousness

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Interestingly, general anesthetics are gap junction blockers (Wentlandt et al., 2006): consistent with the cognitive scaling example above, shutting down electrical communication among the cells leads to a disappearance of the higher-level computational layer while the cellular network is disrupted.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds”, Frontiers in systems neuroscience (2022), doi:10.3389/fnsys.2022.768201; section “Consciousness”. Scope: Anesthetized plants, Hydra and animals including humans

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-tame-32: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.55

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Anesthetic effects on junctions, viability, and integrated behavior can be analyzed in public pharmacological literature and databases. These data cannot uniquely attribute anesthesia to junction blockade or empirically establish dissolution of a Self.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure gap-junction conductance and integrated organism-level responsiveness before, during, and after anesthetic exposure across taxa, testing whether junction blockade mediates behavioral suppression while cell viability remains intact.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Disappearance of a higher-level Self is not independently measurable.

General anesthetics have many molecular targets besides gap junctions.

Anesthesia endpoints differ greatly among plants, Hydra, and humans.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.72
data adequacy: 0.42
operationalizability: 0.55
discriminating power: 0.4
analysis feasibility: 0.62

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Pharmacology databases can test whether general anesthetics inhibit connexins, and at what concentration relative to their main targets. That addresses the gap-junction-blocker clause and can fail it for agents whose clinical action is elsewhere. Loss of a higher-level Self, and anesthesia by gap-junction block from plants to humans, is only partly represented by those ligand tables.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare anesthetic potency at connexins with potency at primary targets such as GABA-A receptors, and test whether selective gap-junction blockers stop organism-level behavior in plants, Hydra, and animals while cell viability remains.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Behavioral arrest in plants and Hydra is in a few papers, not in these pharmacology databases.

Disappearance of a higher-level Self is not a variable separate from loss of coordinated behavior.

Many anesthetics act on synaptic receptors at concentrations below those reported for connexin block.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.65
operationalizability: 0.55
discriminating power: 0.4
analysis feasibility: 0.6
data adequacy: 0.45
